sample_unit: patients (479 risk-based treatment patients matched to 1437 historical controls)

links.outcome: Acute kidney injury and 30-day readmission after colorectal surgery with vs without risk platform
links.effect: AKI fell 2.5% (11.3% to 8.8%) and readmissions fell 3.1% (12% to 8.9%) versus a propensity-matched historical cohort; non-randomized, retrospective design.
links.quote: Utilization of the risk-based management platform was associated with a 2.5% decrease in the rate of acute kidney injury (11.3% to 8.8%) and 3.1% decrease in rate of readmissions (12% to 8.9%).

links.outcome: Outcomes when risk predictions were paired with stratified interventions to route patient management
links.effect: Risk stratification paired with stratified interventions was associated with reduced AKI (11.3% to 8.8%) and readmission (12% to 8.9%) versus matched historical controls.
links.quote: In this study, we found significant reductions in postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) and unplanned readmissions after the implementation of an algorithm based clinical decision support tool that risk-stratified populations and offered stratified interventions.

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world clinical impact of deploying an EHR-integrated surgical risk prediction platform paired with interventions compared to a historical pre-implementation cohort.
